data.name: Geoffrey
data.gender_notes: Geoffrey is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Geoffrey is derived from the Old Testament Hebrew name 'Godefroi' or 'Geoffroi'. It is composed of 'Geoff' meaning 'God' and 'Frey' meaning 'strength'. The name was popular among the Normans in France and was brought to England by the Normans in 1066 AD. The name Geoffrey carries the meaning “God of my strength” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Geoffrey usually hope their child will grow to embody god of my strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: This name signifies a strong connection with God and a belief in His power.
data.etymology: Geoffrey belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of my strength.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Geoffrey total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: ג'פרי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ג'פרי הוא שם שמקורו בשם העברי 'גופר' או 'גאפר', שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא השלום האגואי שלי'. השם עבר דרך השפה היוונית והלטינית, והוא קשור קשר הדוק למושג השלום והאמונה הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Τζέφρυ
in_greek.meaning: ο Θεός είναι η ειρήνη μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Τζέφρυ προέρχεται από το γερμανικό όνομα 'Gottfried', που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός είναι η ειρήνη μου'. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της ειρήνης και της πίστης στον Θεό, και ήταν δημοφιλές στην Εκκλησία την εποχή του Μεσαίωνα.

in_latin.name: Geoffrey
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen 'Geoffrey' originem habet in germanico nomine 'Gottfried', quod significat 'Deus est pax mea'. Nomen hoc erat usitatum in Ecclesia durante Medio Aevo et coniungitur cum conceptu pacis et fidei in Deum.

in_english.name: Geoffrey
in_english.long_meaning: The name Geoffrey originates from the Germanic name 'Gottfried', meaning 'God's peace' or 'divine peace'. It is derived from the Old High German words 'god' (good) and 'frid' (peace). The name has been used in Christian tradition, symbolizing a person who brings peace and harmony. Historically, it was popularized in medieval Europe and remains a significant name in Christian cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name Geoffrey was widely used among the European nobility and clergy in the Middle Ages. It was also the name of several saints, including St. Geoffrey of Orléans and St. Geoffrey of Tours. The name was also associated with the legends of King Arthur and Sir Gawain, who were believed to be named Geoffrey and Geoffrey respectively in some versions of the Arthurian legends.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Geoffrey holds a spiritual significance as it is derived from the Old Testament Hebrew name 'Godefroi' or 'Geoffroi'. The name reaffirms the deep commitment to God and the strength derived from faith. It serves as a reminder of the importance of trusting in God's strength and guidance in times of uncertainty and difficulty. Additionally, the name Geoffrey has been associated with several saints, highlighting the spiritual virtue and virtue of faith, bravery, and strength.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Symbolically, the name Geoffrey means "pledge of God" or "God's warrior." Spiritually, it represents a commitment to God and a call to serve Him courageously in all aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: Geoffrey of Monmouth, a 12th-century Welsh historian and author, wrote a famous work called 'History of the Kings of Britain'.
Historical records show that Saint Geoffrey of Anjouan, a 16th-century French missionary, is venerated as a saint in Madagascar. The name Geoffrey carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
